newsitem.title: USA: ADM declines comment on indictments.
newsitem.headline: ADM declines comment on indictments.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co said Tuesday it will refrain from commenting on indictments against former company officials on charges of allegedly conspiring to fix lysine prices.
"Respecting that the issues will now, finally, be aired in a court of law, we will continue to refrain from comment until the judicial process is complete," ADM said in a statement.
Earlier today, the U.S. Justice Department said a federal grand jury in Chicago indicted three former top ADM executives.

The indictments named Michael Andreas, a former executive vice president and vice chairman of the company; Terrance Wilson, a former group vice president, and Mark Whitacre, who had been fired as head of ADM's BioProducts in August, 1995.
Michael Andreas is also the son of Chairman Dwayne Andreas.
Whitacre acted as an informant for three years in the Justice department's probe of possible price-fixing in the feed and food additives industries.
In October, ADM pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing and agreed to pay $100 million in fines.

In October, ADM said Michael Andreas was taking a temporary administrative leave and Wilson retired for medical reasons. Later that month, ADM announced several executive changes, including a new vice chairman, Gaylord Coan, a board member.
In its statement issued today, ADM said it was responding to the indictments of Michael Andreas and Wilson. No mention was made of Whitacre in the statement.

"We respect this country's judicial system and we fully expect that all responsible individuals will join us in reserving judgment until the legal proceedings have run their course," ADM said. "Both individuals (Michael Andreas and Wilson) provided many years of valuable service to the company and in doing so greatly benefited our employees, customers, shareholders, and the communities of which we are a part. They will now defend themselves and we offer our continued support."
ADM said the agreement it reached previously with the U.S. government should not be interpreted as indicating that these individuals are guilty.
"In fact, the agreement makes no reference whatsoever concerning any involvement of either individual," ADM said.
